text: Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Waltrick.
Good evening. Let me see. Waltrick, two guests, fourteen nights. Do you have your passport?
Here it is. We booked a double room with breakfast.
That is right. I am very sorry, but the room is not ready yet. There was a problem with the air conditioning.
How long is it going to take? It is almost one in the morning.
About thirty minutes. I can offer you a room on the second floor right now, if you prefer.
I would rather wait and have the room we booked. Is there somewhere we can sit?
Of course. The bar is open, and coffee is on us tonight. I will come and find you.
Hi, I have a reservation under the name Waltrick.
I would rather have a room on a higher floor.
Sorry, my key card is not working.

I have worked at a front desk for eleven years, and I ask every single guest the same two things: a name for the reservation, and a document, usually a passport. That is all I need to start. What surprises me is what guests do not do. They are afraid of asking for things. They stand there, they take the key card, they go up, and then they sleep badly for two weeks because the room faces the road. Most of what people want from a hotel is free and takes me thirty seconds. A higher floor. A quieter side. A late check-out on the last day. Bags kept behind the desk before three o'clock. I cannot offer what nobody asks for. If the hotel is not full, I almost never say no to a different floor. So please, ask. The worst thing I can say is that we are full tonight.

The first room they gave me was right next to the elevator. Every time somebody went up or down, I heard the doors, and people talk in the corridor at two in the morning as if it were the afternoon. The first night I said nothing. The second night I said nothing again, and I did not sleep at all. On the third day I finally went down to the front desk and I said, I am sorry, my room is very noisy because it is next to the elevator. Could I change to another room, please. The woman looked at her screen for about ten seconds and gave me a key card for a room at the end of the corridor. The whole conversation took two minutes. Two minutes, after two nights without sleep. That is the part that still annoys me.
